                    ### Question
                    Which of the following causes of malabsorption occurs with alteration of the intestinal mucosa ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. The Crigler-Najjar syndrome.
opb. A cholestasis
opc. Celiac disease
opd. Achalasia

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Celiac disease is a condition where ingestion of gluten triggers an immune response that damages the intestinal mucosa, leading to malabsorption. This aligns with the consensus that celiac disease causes malabsorption through alteration of the intestinal mucosa. Crigler-Najjar syndrome involves bilirubin metabolism and does not affect the intestinal mucosa, making it an unlikely cause of malabsorption. Cholestasis results in impaired fat digestion due to bile flow obstruction but does not directly alter the intestinal mucosa, thus it is not primarily associated with mucosal damage. Achalasia is an esophageal motility disorder affecting swallowing and does not involve the intestinal mucosa, making it an unlikely cause of malabsorption. The evidence paths confirm that celiac disease is associated with inflammation due to gluten, supporting its role in mucosal damage and malabsorption.
